\subsection*{Randomized --- PTM: Results}

\begin{definition}[Complementing machine output]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.flipOutput}
\label{Turing.NDTM.flipOutput}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NDTM}
Given a nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean output symbols, and
state set $Q$, form a machine with the same initial state and transition behavior except
that every emitted output symbol is replaced by its Boolean complement. The machine's
choice bit, input-head movement, work-tape actions, and successor state remain those
specified by the original transition.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Complementing configuration output]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.flipCfg}
\label{Turing.NDTM.flipCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg}
Given a configuration of a machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean symbols, state set $Q$,
and fixed Boolean input string $x$, form the configuration with the same state,
input-head position, work-tape contents, and work-tape head positions, but with every
Boolean symbol on the output tape complemented.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Flipped output after one step]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.flipOutput_stepWith}
\label{Turing.NDTM.flipOutput_stepWith}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.flipCfg, Turing.NDTM.flipOutput, Turing.NDTM.stepWith, Turing.NDTM.stepWith_of_halt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols and $k$ work tapes,
let $b$ be a Boolean choice, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $c$ be a
configuration on $x$. Taking one step under $b$ with the machine whose output symbols
are flipped, starting from the configuration obtained by flipping every output bit of
$c$, gives the configuration obtained by flipping every output bit of the result of
taking one step under $b$ with $M$ from $c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Flipped output after a run]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.flipOutput_runWith}
\label{Turing.NDTM.flipOutput_runWith}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.flipCfg, Turing.NDTM.flipOutput, Turing.NDTM.flipOutput_stepWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols and $k$ work tapes,
let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $w$ be a Boolean choice word, and let $c$ be a
configuration on $x$. Running the machine with flipped output on the configuration
obtained by flipping every output bit of $c$ gives the configuration obtained by
flipping every output bit of the result of running $M$ from $c$ under $w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Flipped output at initialization]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.flipOutput_initCfg}
\label{Turing.NDTM.flipOutput_initCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.flipCfg, Turing.NDTM.flipOutput, Turing.NDTM.initCfg}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols and $k$ work tapes,
and let $x$ be a Boolean input word. The initial configuration of the machine whose
output symbols are flipped, on input $x$, equals the configuration obtained by flipping
every output bit in the initial configuration of $M$ on $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Complementing a finite nondeterministic machine]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.flipOutput}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.flipOutput}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.NDTM.flipOutput}
Given a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, form a finite
nondeterministic machine with the same number of work tapes, the same finite state set,
and the same initial state, whose transitions complement every Boolean symbol they emit
and otherwise preserve the original transition behavior.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Running in time]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.RunsInTime}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p021-b003,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p021-b005
}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.RunsInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin}
A finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols runs within time bound $T$
if, for every Boolean input string $x$, it halts within $T(|x|)$ steps.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Output for a choice string]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
For a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over Boolean symbols, a Boolean input
string $x$, and a Boolean choice string $w$, let the output be the output tape contents
after running $N$ with choice string $w$ from its initial configuration on input $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Probability of a specified output]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.randProb, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith}
For a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over Boolean symbols, Boolean strings
$x$ and $v$, and a natural number $t$, the output probability is the probability, under
the length-$t$ random choice distribution, that running $N$ on $x$ with the random
choice string produces exactly $v$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Bounded-error probabilistic decision in time]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInTime}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p023-b001}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p002-b003}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $L$
be a language of Boolean strings, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. The machine
decides $L$ with bounded error within time $T$ if, on every input $x$, it halts within
$T(|x|)$ steps and its output equals the indicator of membership in $L$ with probability
at least $2/3$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One-sided randomized decision in time]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTime}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p021-b006}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p006-b003}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $L$
be a language of Boolean strings, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. On every input
$x$, the machine halts within $T(|x|)$ steps. If $x\in L$, it outputs true with
probability at least $2/3$; if $x\notin L$, then for every choice string of length
$T(|x|)$ it outputs the one-symbol string false.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Decision implies bounded halting]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInTime.runsInTime}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInTime.runsInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInTime, Turing.FinNDTM.RunsInTime}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be
a language of binary strings, and let $T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. If $N$ halts on
every branch within $T(|x|)$ steps and outputs the membership indicator for $L$ with
probability at least $2/3$ on every binary input $x$, then $N$ halts on every branch
within $T(|x|)$ steps for every binary input.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One-sided-error machines halt within the time bound]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTime.runsInTime}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTime.runsInTime}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTime, Turing.FinNDTM.RunsInTime}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be
a language of binary strings, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. If, on every input
$x$, every branch halts within $T(|x|)$ steps, output $1$ has probability at least $2/3$
when $x\in L$, and every branch outputs $0$ when $x\notin L$, then every branch halts
within $T(|x|)$ steps on every input.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Runs stabilize after guaranteed halting]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.runWith_eq_runWith_take}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.runWith_eq_runWith_take}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $x$ be
a binary input, and let $t\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose every choice word of length exactly
$t$ leads to a halted configuration on $x$. Then for every choice word $w$ with $|w|\geq
t$, running on $w$ gives the same configuration as running on the prefix of $w$ of
length $t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Output probability after guaranteed halting]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb_eq_of_haltsWithin}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb_eq_of_haltsWithin}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.randProb_congr, Randomized.randProb_take, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith, Turing.FinNDTM.runWith_eq_runWith_take, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $x$ be
a binary input, and let $t,t'\in\mathbb{N}$ with $t\le t'$. If every choice word of
length exactly $t$ leads to a halted configuration on input $x$, then for every binary
output word $v$, the probability of outputting $v$ after $t'$ choices equals the
probability of outputting $v$ after $t$ choices.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Certain output has probability one]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb_eq_one}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb_eq_one}
\leanok

\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $x$ be
a binary input, and let $t\in\mathbb{N}$. If every choice word of length exactly $t$
produces the same output $v$, then the probability of outputting $v$ after $t$ choices
is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positive Output Probability Gives a Witness]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.exists_outputWith_of_outputProb_pos}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.exists_outputWith_of_outputProb_pos}
\leanok

\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, and
let $x,v$ be binary words and $t\in\mathbb{N}$. If the fraction of length-$t$ choice
words on which $N$ outputs $v$ is positive, then some length-$t$ choice word makes $N$
output exactly $v$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity in the time bound]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInTime.mono}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInTime.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInTime, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb_eq_of_haltsWithin, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin.mono}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be
a language of binary strings, and let $T_1,T_2\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ satisfy
$T_1(m)\le T_2(m)$ for every $m$. If $N$ halts within $T_1(|x|)$ steps on every branch
and outputs the membership indicator for $L$ with probability at least $2/3$ on every
input $x$, then it also has these properties with time bound $T_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of the time bound]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTime.mono}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTime.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTime, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb_eq_of_haltsWithin, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith, Turing.FinNDTM.runWith_eq_runWith_take, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin.mono}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be
a language of binary strings, and let $T_1,T_2:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ satisfy
$T_1(n)\le T_2(n)$ for every $n$. If $N$ satisfies the stated one-sided-error decision
condition for $L$ within time $T_1$, then it satisfies that condition within time $T_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded error from one-sided error]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTime.bpDecidesInTime}

\leanok

\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be
a language of binary strings, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that on every

\begin{theorem}[Output Flipping Preserves Halting]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.flipOutput_haltsWithin_iff}

\leanok

\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, and
let $x$ be a binary input and $t\in\mathbb{N}$. The machine obtained from $N$ by
complementing each bit it emits halts on $x$ within $t$ steps along every branch if and
only if $N$ does.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.flipOutput_outputWith}

\leanok

\begin{theorem}[Output flipping preserves bounded-error decision]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInTime.flipOutput}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInTime.flipOutput}
\leanok

\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be
a language of binary strings, and let $T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. If $N$ halts

every Boolean symbol it outputs halts within the same time and outputs the indicator of

\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Bounded-error randomized time]
\lean{Randomized.BPTIME}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p023-b001}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p002-b003}
\label{Randomized.BPTIME}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInTime}
For a time bound $T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, the class $\mathrm{BPTIME}(T)$
consists of all languages over the Boolean alphabet for which there are a constant
$c\in\mathbb{N}$ and a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine that decides the
language with bounded error in time at most $cT(n)$ on inputs of length $n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Polynomial-time bounded-error languages]
\lean{Randomized.BPP_PTM}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p023-b001}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p003-b003}
\label{Randomized.BPP_PTM}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPTIME}
The class $\mathrm{BPP}_{\mathrm{PTM}}$ is the union, over all $c\in\mathbb{N}$, of the
classes $\mathrm{BPTIME}(n^c+1)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Randomized time]
\lean{Randomized.RTIME}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p021-b006}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p006-b003}
\label{Randomized.RTIME}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTime}
For a time bound $T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, the class $\mathrm{RTIME}(T)$
consists of all languages over the Boolean alphabet for which there are a constant
$c\in\mathbb{N}$ and a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine that recognizes the
language with one-sided error in time at most $cT(n)$ on inputs of length $n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Polynomial-time one-sided randomized languages]
\lean{Randomized.RP_PTM}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p021-b006}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p006-b003}
\label{Randomized.RP_PTM}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RTIME}
The class $\mathrm{RP}_{\mathrm{PTM}}$ is the union, over all $c\in\mathbb{N}$, of the
classes $\mathrm{RTIME}(n^c+1)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Complement of the RP language class]
\lean{Randomized.coRP_PTM}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p022-b003}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch07-randomized-computation}{pdf-26d95080dbde-p006-b004}
\label{Randomized.coRP_PTM}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RP_PTM}
The class of co-RP languages for probabilistic Turing machines consists of all languages
over the Boolean alphabet whose complements belong to the RP language class for
probabilistic Turing machines.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of randomized time]
\lean{Randomized.BPTIME.mono}
\label{Randomized.BPTIME.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPTIME, Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInTime.mono}
\difficulty{4}
Let $T_1,T_2:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $T_1(n)\le T_2(n)$ for every $n$. Then
every language decidable by a bounded-error randomized Turing machine in time bounded by
a constant multiple of $T_1$ belongs to the corresponding class with time bounded by a
constant multiple of $T_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of randomized time]
\lean{Randomized.RTIME.mono}
\label{Randomized.RTIME.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RTIME, Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTime.mono}
\difficulty{4}
Let $T_1,T_2 : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $T_1(n) \le T_2(n)$ for every $n$.
Then every language in $\mathrm{RTIME}(T_1)$ belongs to $\mathrm{RTIME}(T_2)$, where
membership means that a finite randomized machine halts on every branch within a
constant multiple of the time bound, accepts members with probability at least $2/3$,
and never accepts nonmembers.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Constant-factor scaling of randomized time]
\lean{Randomized.BPTIME_const_mul_subset}
\label{Randomized.BPTIME_const_mul_subset}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPTIME}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $a$ and time bound $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, every
language decidable with bounded error in time bounded by a constant multiple of $n
\mapsto aT(n)$ is decidable with bounded error in time bounded by a constant multiple of
$T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Absorbing a constant time factor]
\lean{Randomized.RTIME_const_mul_subset}
\label{Randomized.RTIME_const_mul_subset}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RTIME}
\difficulty{3}
For every $a \in \mathbb{N}$ and every function $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$,
$\mathrm{RTIME}(n \mapsto aT(n)) \subseteq \mathrm{RTIME}(T)$, where the time classes
allow an arbitrary constant multiplicative factor in their bounds and require randomized
machines to halt on every branch, accept members with probability at least $2/3$, and
never accept nonmembers.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Randomized time is contained in bounded-error time]
\lean{Randomized.RTIME_subset_BPTIME}
\label{Randomized.RTIME_subset_BPTIME}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPTIME, Randomized.RTIME, Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInTime.bpDecidesInTime}
\difficulty{1}
For every function $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $\mathrm{RTIME}(T) \subseteq
\mathrm{BPTIME}(T)$. Both classes allow a finite randomized machine running in time
bounded by a constant multiple of $T$; in $\mathrm{RTIME}(T)$ it halts on every branch,
accepts members with probability at least $2/3$, and never accepts nonmembers, while in
$\mathrm{BPTIME}(T)$ it outputs the correct membership bit with probability at least
$2/3$ on every input.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Complement closure of bounded-time randomized computation]
\lean{Randomized.compl_mem_BPTIME}
\label{Randomized.compl_mem_BPTIME}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPTIME, Turing.FinNDTM.BPDecidesInTime.flipOutput, Turing.FinNDTM.flipOutput}
\difficulty{1}
Let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be any time bound and let $L$ be a language over the
Boolean alphabet. If $L$ belongs to BPTIME$(T)$, then its complement also belongs to
BPTIME$(T)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Closure of BPP under complement]
\lean{Randomized.compl_mem_BPP_PTM}
\label{Randomized.compl_mem_BPP_PTM}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.BPP_PTM, Randomized.compl_mem_BPTIME}
\difficulty{3}
For every language $L$ over the Boolean alphabet, if $L$ belongs to BPP, then its
complement belongs to BPP.
\end{theorem}
